text:
maya: heads up — started seeing a sharp uptick in 95/99 latency on dedicated pool after yesterday's AWQ act-quant group-size tweak on redwood-3b-awq

carlos: saw perf noise around 06:12 UTC too, p99 jumped from ~180ms -> ~420ms on batch sizes >8

aj: any quality regressions or just latency?

maya: both. some samples show token-level stutter and a few completions with repeat loops. eval BLEU/ROUGE small delta but manual inspection flagged more repeats

ranjit: quick summary of diff: group_size 64 -> 96, act_quant=true. change landed in canary and then propagated to dedicated pool via autoscale policy last night

maya: adding logs snippet from the runner, repeating chunk every ~30 tokens: 
```
[2026-02-25T06:12:03Z] INFO runner: decoding loop detected reset at step=142, kv_cache_len=158
[2026-02-25T06:12:03Z] WARN runner: sustained send latency >100ms for shard=3
```

carlos: hmm looks like KV cache eviction thrashing maybe due to group_size jump. When group is bigger, memory layout/alignments change and some kernels fallback

aj: can we reproduce in staging with same traffic mix? I can spin a dedicated canary with group_size=96 and act_quant=true and run the regen suite

maya: repro is flaky but I got one failing sample locally with seed 42. Pasted prompt+output in gist: https://rwd.gist/p/4f2c (internal)

ranjit: also noticed scheduler logs show uneven placement across GPUs after the change. Some instances got 3x batchpack merges which increased per-request batching latency

carlos: proposed mitigation: rollback group_size -> 64 and keep act_quant=true; monitor for 1 full peak window. If rollback reduces latency then we know it's group-size related

aj: agree. I'll prepare rollback PR and a canary with metrics: p50/p95/p99, gen tokens/s, repeat-rate, and sample-level BLEU. Can we tag requests to route a % to the canary?

deploy-bot: deploy initiated by aj: rollback awq-group-size -> 64 on pool=dedicated-west-1, canary=10%

maya: thanks. also want to run a focused eval: vary group_size in [48,56,64,80,96] with act_quant on and off, measure latency, repeat-rate, and sample entropy. I suspect a threshold at ~80 where kernel fallback begins

ranjit: good idea. I can add a micro-benchmark that exercises long-prefix streaming and variable sequence lengths; that should surface KV eviction patterns

sre-bot: alert muted for awq-latency-spike; alert owner=eng-ml, until=2026-02-25T10:00:00Z

carlos: quick note — if rollback doesn't help we'll try per-request routing to a lower-quant model as fallback (redwood-3b-fp8) to keep quality stable while we debug

maya: update: 20m after canary deploy p99 down to ~210ms (was 420). repeat-rate on sampled traces dropped from 6.2% -> 1.1%. keeping an eye for edge backlog

aj: nice. I'll run the sweep later today and post aggregated plots. tagging @ranjit for scheduler traces and @carlos for kernel fallback logs

ranjit: copying scheduler trace snippet for debug: 
```
placement: shard0->gpu1, shard1->gpu2, shard2->gpu1, shard3->gpu1
merged_batches: 3
kv_evictions: 12
```

maya: great work — next steps: full sweep, hypothesis test for kernel fallback at group_size>=80, and plan for safe stable group defaults. Will open an RFC after the sweep with recommended defaults per model/seq-len

carlos: +1, also add a guard in runtime to limit merged batch depth per-shard as a kill-switch for noisy kernels

maya: thanks team :thumbsup:
